title: Magnitude, unit & position vectors
examples: How do I find the unit vector if I know the coordinates?
What is the difference between a position vector and a general vector?
Can you show me an example of finding a vector parallel to another one?

explain.say: Today we look at vector magnitude and unit vectors. We will learn how to find the length of a vector.
The magnitude is simply the length of the vector. If a vector is three units right and four units up, its magnitude is five.
Next we cover unit vectors. A unit vector has a magnitude of exactly one. We find it by dividing the vector by its own magnitude.

items: Result is the unit vector u

explain.say: For example, if a vector is two i plus two j, its magnitude is two times the square root of two. The unit vector is then one i plus one j over the square root of two.

items: Divide v by |v| to get u = (2i + 2j) / (2√2)

explain.say: Finally, we find a vector parallel to another. We just multiply the original vector by a scalar constant. This keeps the direction the same.

items: Multiply v by a scalar constant k
Result is the parallel vector k v

faq.q: What is the difference between a vector and a scalar?
faq.a: A scalar only has size or magnitude. A vector has both size and direction, which is why we use i j k.
asks: What does it mean for a vector to have direction?
Are vectors just numbers with arrows?

faq.q: How do I find the unit vector if I know the coordinates?
faq.a: First, find the magnitude using the Pythagorean theorem. Then, divide each component by that magnitude.
asks: What is the formula for a unit vector?
If my vector is (6, 8), what is the unit vector?

faq.a: A position vector points from the origin to a specific point. It uses the coordinates of that point directly.
asks: Does the position vector start at the origin?

faq.q: Why do I need to find a vector parallel to another?
faq.a: This is useful when you need a vector pointing in the same direction but perhaps a different length. You just scale it up or down.
asks: If I multiply a vector by 3, what happens to its direction?

faq.q: If I find the unit vector, is it always a simple number?
faq.a: No, it is usually a combination of i j and k components. Its magnitude, however, will always be one.
asks: Can the unit vector have negative components?
Is the unit vector always written with i j k?

facts: The magnitude of a vector v = x i + y j is calculated as the square root of x squared plus y squared.
A unit vector always has a magnitude equal to one.
To find a unit vector, you divide the original vector by its magnitude.
A vector parallel to another vector is found by multiplying the original vector by a non-zero scalar.

quiz.say: If v = 6 i + 8 j, what is the magnitude of v?
quiz.why: You use the Pythagorean theorem on the components six and eight to find the length, which is ten.

wrong.0: You incorrectly calculated the sum of the squares without taking the square root.
wrong.2: You incorrectly added the components together instead of squaring and summing them.
wrong.3: You only added the components without squaring them at all.

quiz.say: What is the unit vector in the direction of v = 3 i + 4 j?
quiz.why: The magnitude is five, so you divide both components three divided by five and four divided by five.

wrong.0: You incorrectly scaled only the first component by the magnitude.
wrong.2: You forgot to divide the vector by its magnitude of five.
wrong.3: This is a common mistake when assuming the components must be equal.

quiz.say: If w is parallel to v = 2 i + 3 j, and w = 4 i + 6 j, what is the scalar multiplier?
quiz.why: You can see that both components of w are exactly two times the corresponding components of v.

wrong.0: You treated the resulting vector as the multiplier instead of a single number.
wrong.1: You only compared the first components to find the multiplier.
wrong.3: This would mean the vector w is identical to the vector v.
